newsitem.title: UK: Vendome sterling profit down in year.
newsitem.headline: Vendome sterling profit down in year.

text.p: Luxury goods maker Vendome Luxury Goods Plc on Tuesday said its pretax profits for the year ended March 31 fell to 247.5 million pounds ($412.8 million) from 257.7 million in the previous year as strong sterling took its toll.
It said it raised its total dividend by 1.6 percent in sterling terms to 10.4 pence. In Swiss francs, the pretax profit actually increased by 8.1 percent to 509.9 million.

Vendome is 70 percent owned by South African-controlled Richemont Securities and was created three years ago from the rationalisation of Richemont AG, Dunhill Holdings and Rothmans International. Its shares are traded in London.

Chairman Joseph Kanoui said the results were "broadly satisfactory" and reflected growth in all major markets, despite lower tourist spending in the Far East which "particularly affected the margins and profits of those of our brands which have a greater proportion of their sales in the region".
Among the watch brands included in Vendome's portfolio are Vacheron Constantin, the oldest Swiss watchmaker, Cartier, Piaget and Baume & Mercier.
On Tuesday, Vendome said it has ended its relationship with well-known German fashion designer Karl Lagerfeld. The rights of the Karl Lagerfeld trademark will be transferred to Lagerfeld, it said.
"There will be no significant effect on the results of the Group in the current year as a result of this agreement," the company said.
Vendome said the second half of the year showed "significant increases in turnover and operating profits, with a marked improvement in underlying demand complemented by favourable currency effects".
It said the second half improvement is of "great encouragement" for the coming year.
"Performance so far in the year, for the Group as a whole, has been encouraging and turnover and profits should continue on a positive trend." ($ = 0.599 British Pounds)
